The adopter is then to be unluited from the neck of the leaden tube, if the operator choofes ; and in order that no vapour may escape into the workhop, a bit of lute or a cork may be applied to the beak of the adopter. <x_0.29><y_0.4313>" Nevertheless, as the lutes which connect the adopter with the retort are fomewhat followed towards the end of the operation, it would be more prudent to leave every thing in its place, for fear of deranging those lutes. This danger is greater when the adopter is of lead, because the great length of this additional piece tends to force the luting fill more on that account. If it be required to proceed immediately to a new diftillation, the retort or bottle with its capfule or pan muft be immediately taken from the furnace, and another fabilituted in its place ready prepared during the former diftillation.
